# Door panel removal for tinting or access

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Open the door, remove covers and screws, then pry off the entire door panel starting from the bottom. [t943]

[Partial] Remove the door handle assembly and locate any sheetrock screws or other unique hardware holding interior trim pieces. [t943]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Open the door.
2. Remove the small rubber or plastic cover on the armrest by gently prying up at the gaps around it.
3. Unscrew a single 10mm bolt from behind the removed armrest cover (often requiring a Phillips head).
4. Pry off the front switch cover using the same method as the rear armrest.
5. Remove screws holding the switches to their panel trim, then feed the switches through when pulling the main door panel away.
6. Trim under the door latch by prying at the seam where a front and back piece meet.
7. [Partial] Unscrew two 10mm golden screws located after removing the lower covers.
8. Pry off the entire door panel starting from the bottom, working around the perimeter to release plastic clips spaced roughly 9 inches apart.
9. Lift the top portion of the panel slightly while pulling outward until it releases.

_Procedure reported by [t943]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/simple-how-to-door-panel-removal.3693/>_

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t943] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Remove the door handle assembly to expose hidden fasteners.
2. [Partial] Locate any sheetrock screws or other unique hardware holding interior trim pieces.

</details>

## Tools

- Small flathead screwdriver [t943]
- [Partial] Phillips screwdriver or plastic pry tool [t943]
- 10mm socket and 1/4-inch ratchet [t943]

## Tips & gotchas

- Take your time when prying to avoid damage. [t943]
- Start at the bottom of the door panel and work upward. [t943]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Forgetting that pulling outward is key rather than just lifting up. [t943]
- [Partial] Overlooking sheetrock screws used for custom interior trim like rubber elbow pads. [t943]
